_note: accessibleTable - the differentiator, and the reason it is CHEAP: the data is already structured, <Table> already exists, so a blind user gets the numbers, a sighted user gets the chart, and the author writes one element. Default ON. The pivot is the whole trick: a multi-series chart becomes one row per x with one column per series, in FIRST APPEARANCE order on both axes (never sorted, because the author's row order is the author's intent). A missing (x, series) cell is an EMPTY STRING, never a zero - a datum that was not measured is not a measurement of nothing. A duplicate (x, series) pair is last-wins. The `summary` line is the same sentence the figure's aria-label already speaks, so the two can never drift apart.
